newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Chile's Quebrada Blanca says unions to play tough.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Quebrada Blanca says unions to play tough.

text.p: Workers at Cominco Ltd's Quebrada Blanca copper mine in Chile will probably reject a final wage offer at a vote Sunday but will not necessarily strike, the firm's general manager said Wednesday.

Chilean law forbids any strike to begin for at least three days after a vote to stop work, and workers will probably want to use this period to put pressure on the company, Quebrada Blanca's James Drake told Reuters by telephone from Santiago.

"It's all part of the standard Chilean procedures. Once they vote for a strike they have three days of final negotiations before they can legally begin the strike," Drake said. "So typically it goes to a strike vote. That's really where the final negotiations take place."
Quebrada Blanca will present later Wednesday its final wage offer before Sunday's scheduled strike vote, Drake said.
Unions and management have agreed not to reveal details of wage offers during negotiations.
It was not immediately possible to contact union officials.
Canadian-owned Quebrada Blanca, which has been in wage negotiations since mid-March, produces about 75,000 tonnes of copper in cathodes a year at a mine near the Bolivian border.
The mine's workforce went on strike for a week while negotiating their previous labor contracts two-and-a-half years ago.
About 70 percent of the mine's workforce of 500 people is unionized.
